findings.claim: When diagnoseNextRecommendationRejection finds an enum rejection anywhere in the validation error tree, the returned error entirely replaces the original err (fmt.Errorf with %s, not %w, and no reference to err at all) instead of augmenting it, so any other concurrent schema violation on the same instance (e.g. an unknown top-level property, since the schema root sets additionalProperties:false) is silently dropped from the reported message even though the underlying jsonschema.ValidationError still carries it as a sibling Cause.
proof_refs: tools/entry-contract-validator/main.go:185-189: the new branch `if diagnostic, ok := diagnoseNextRecommendationRejection(err); ok { return &contractError{code: exitSchemaValidation, err: fmt.Errorf("schema validation: %s", diagnostic)} }` returns before reaching the pre-existing `fmt.Errorf("schema validation: %w", err)` fallback, so the diagnostic string is the only detail surfaced whenever the match succeeds

tools/entry-contract-validator/main.go:229-243: findEnumRejection returns on the first matching Cause found anywhere in the tree and never inspects sibling Causes, so an unrelated violation elsewhere in the same instance is never surfaced once the token match is found

skills/_shared/entry-contract.schema.json:7 sets root `"additionalProperties": false`, so an instance with both an unknown top-level property and an invalid expected_native_next_recommendation token is a real, constructible input that would trigger this masking
no test added in this diff (main_test.go or token_domain_test.go) constructs an instance with two simultaneous violations, so this loss of diagnostic completeness is uncovered
